newsitem.title: USA: Northwest seeks sanctions against Japan.
newsitem.headline: Northwest seeks sanctions against Japan.

text.p: Northwest Airlines Corp. said on Thursday it asked the Transportation Department to impose sanctions on Japan for Japan's refusal to allow it to fly a new route that was to begin last July 1.
Northwest said it asked the department to enforce a complaint it filed last July 3 after Japan declined to permit it to start a Seattle-Osaka-Jakarta service.
The carrier said Japan's continued refusal to authorize the service was a clear violation of the U.S.-Japan air transport agreement and warranted sanctions under U.S. law.
It called for immediate department action.
Northwest said that an appropriate sanction would be a denial of a request by Japan Airlines Co. Ltd. for new passenger-cargo flights from Tokyo to Kona, Hawaii.
Richard Hirst, Northwest's senior vice president for corporate affairs, said the United States had met informally with Japan this month on the issue, but with no results.
"It is apparent that Japan has no intention to honor its bilateral obligations, and that imposition of sanctions is necessary," Hirst said.
The Transportation Department had no immediate comment.
